Blue Ridge B Quezon City, Philippines Dear SB Member Reyes: This has reference to your letter dated 22 May 2018 requesting for the Department's opinion on the issue of whether or not public funds of a barangay can be legally used for projects, programs, activities, and services for the benefit of registered voters who are no longer residents of the said barangay. In the said letter, it is stated that a large group of informal settlers, who used to reside in Barangay Blue Ridge B, Quezon City (Barangay), were relocated to Rodriguez (formerly Montalban) and to San Jose del Monte City. Despite the relocation, they remain registered voters of the Barangay. The issue submitted for clarification is whether or not the public funds of the Barangay can be legally used for projects, programs, activities, and services for the benefit of its registered voters who are no longer residents thereat. Republic Act NO. 7160 (RA 7160), otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991, is silent on the matter. Nevertheless, it mentions, in Section 384, the role of the Barangay as implementing unit of government policies, programs and activities in the community, as well as, in Section 391, the powers, duties, and functions of the Sanggunian Barangay which include enacting ordinances for the general welfare of its inhabitants and assisting in establishment of cooperatives for improvement of economic condition and well-being of its residents, among others. Accordingly, Barangay, being a territorial and political subdivision, exercises its role, powers, responsibilities, functions, and authority within its territorial jurisdiction. It is worth mentioning that in the facts given, the registered voters of the Barangay were informal settlers who relocated to different barangays of different cities. We find it material to note that relocated informal settlers do not normally maintain several residences. Thus, the barangay where they transferred and where they are now residents of shall include them in the coverage of its delivery of basic services, programs, policies, projects, and activities. We are of the opinion that the programs, projects, activities, and policies of Barangay Blue Ridge B are for the benefit and general welfare of its residents only. (Emphasis supplied). In other words, public funds of the Barangay can only be used legally for projects, programs,

activities, and services for the benefit of those residing therein. In view of that, our opinion is that residency in a Barangay, regardless if one is a registered voter thereof or not, entitles one to the coverage of the delivery of Barangay programs, projects, activities, and basic services. We hope that we have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, y the authority of the Secreta USEC. TIN B.
